role: Port of ChunkProviderServer (loadChunk, populate four-neighbor rule, unloadChunksIfNotNearSpawn, unloadQueuedChunks), Chunk.populateChunk and PlayerManager (addPlayer, removePlayer, updateMountedMovingPlayer, filterChunkLoadQueue, view radius), including a faithful JDK 8 ConcurrentHashMap bin/TreeBin model so the unload set iterates in Java's order.

structs.name: cl
structs.java: ChunkProviderServer plus PlayerManager plus EntityPlayerMP.loadedChunks for one player

gpu: function cl_unload_step: the unload set is a chunkset (chunkset.c): the drain computes its order once (a sort by bin and list stamp) and walks it while no key is added (lane/gpuorder, L4)

line 1075, functions populate_chunk/load_chunk/populate: mutual recursion (load_chunk -> populate_chunk -> populate -> load_chunk for feed loads, bounded because feed loads pass a pop id and skip the populate rule)
struct cl fields emit, feed.pop_loads, load_cb, unload_cb, client: callbacks through function pointers

the popped list, the send queue, the watchers and the drain's scratch are fixed arrays made with the cl (fixed_array, CU_MAX_BINS, CU_MAX_NODES, CL_MAX_QUEUE, CL_MAX_WATCH, CL_MAX_POP); past one the program stops; is_popped reads a fixed open-addressing index over the popped list (popidx, CL_POP_INDEX, lane/longrun)
notes: Checked against netherite.oracle.ChunkLoadProbe recordings in out/java/chunkload/ (per the header). Population-driven loads still come back as recorded loads through cl_replay_load / cl_pop_load (serverreplay.c) rather than from the populate features themselves in every path. The ConcurrentHashMap model moved to chunkset.c, where the order is carried as data (list stamps). cl_set_send_queue replaces the player's send queue with a snapshot's EntityPlayerMP.loadedChunks. Lane gpuphase (GPU audit L6): cl_digest hashes the provider and player manager for the phase digests (phase.h).
